provenance_of_stored_value.value_source_at_call_site: CreateWindowExA is called through IAT 0x005331B4 at 0x0048F770; its EAX result is moved to ESI at 0x0048F776. EBX was zeroed at 0x0048F53F in the routine at 0x0048F530 (Binary Ninja annotation FX_Igimutex; radare2 label main; the retail name is not established) and is callee-saved across the intervening cdecl calls. The compare at 0x0048F779 (cmp esi, ebx) and jne at 0x0048F77F send a non-null result to 0x0048F790; a null result falls through to the error path at 0x0048F781. On the success path ESI is pushed at 0x0048F79F and the setter is called at 0x0048F7A0. The stored dword is therefore the window handle returned by CreateWindowExA on the success path.

independent_reanalysis.detail: The retail image was re-read byte-exactly with objdump and capstone, then re-analysed with Binary Ninja MCP, radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1. Binary Ninja is the only decompiler used in this corrected pass. The prior Ghidra pass is retained only as superseded historical evidence.

observed_facts.fact: The hashed image is PE32, machine i386, preferred image base 0x00400000, Windows GUI subsystem, .text at VA 0x00401000 with virtual size 0x00132000. SHA-256 is dea34892d417715873ea61d7b2ba5556655f1ad65385104348146f9679915a01 and MD5 is 9d8ebb7f28a1be56a8626dd5948826e4.
The function at 0x0048F0A0 is exactly six bytes, 0x0048F0A0-0x0048F0A5: A1 C4 8B 5C 00 = mov eax, dword [0x005C8BC4], then C3 = ret. The following byte at 0x0048F0A6 is 0x90 padding.
observed_facts.evidence: C2, C9; BN function_info range 0x48f0a0-0x48f0a6; r2 size 6

observed_facts.fact: Binary Ninja reports one basic block, two instructions, zero calls and zero edges. Its decompilation is a single read of g_5c8bc4 returned in EAX.

No arguments are read. The only memory operand is the absolute dword at 0x005C8BC4; there is no ESP/EBP-relative operand. Binary Ninja stack layout contains only __return_addr; radare2 reports stackframe 0 and args 0.
Binary Ninja's prototype is int32_t() with cdecl. The names AppContext_GethWnd and g_5c8bc4 are database annotations, not retail PE symbols; they are not used as evidence of source-level names.

Exactly 20 direct E8 call instructions target 0x0048F0A0: 0x0048FA45, 0x0048FE78, 0x004900AF, 0x00491BED, 0x00491C21, 0x00491C2D, 0x00491C39, 0x00493C30, 0x00493EBB, 0x00493ECF, 0x00494104, 0x00494880, 0x00494891, 0x004948A4, 0x00494E91, 0x00494EA2, 0x00494EB5, 0x0049538B, 0x004988E8, 0x00509B32. Binary Ninja and radare2 both report 20; there are no E9/EB jumps and no stored dword literal equal to 0x0048F0A0 in the file.

Exactly three references to 0x005C8BC4 exist in the image: read at 0x0048F0A0, write at 0x0048F0E4 (setter 0x0048F0E0), read at 0x0048F100. The byte-exact scan finds the four-byte value at file offsets 0x8f0a1, 0x8f0e5 and 0x8f102 (VAs 0x48f0a1, 0x48f0e5, 0x48f102). Binary Ninja's data-xref query returned 0 rows and is not the source of this count.

The setter 0x0048F0E0 is 10 bytes: mov eax,[esp+4]; mov [0x005C8BC4],eax; ret. It is called at 0x0048F7A0. The CreateWindowExA import is at IAT 0x005331B4 and is called at 0x0048F770; its EAX result is moved to ESI at 0x0048F776. EBX was zeroed at 0x0048F53F in the routine at 0x0048F530 (Binary Ninja annotation FX_Igimutex; radare2 label main; the retail name is not established) and is callee-saved across the intervening cdecl calls. The compare at 0x0048F779 (cmp esi,ebx) and jne at 0x0048F77F send a non-null handle to 0x0048F790, while a null result falls through to the error path at 0x0048F781. On the success path ESI is pushed at 0x0048F79F immediately before the setter call.
observed_facts.evidence: C8; CreateWindowExA IAT 0x005331B4 resolved with radare2 import listing; instruction addresses checked with objdump

observed_facts.fact: The third reference 0x0048F100 loads 0x005C8BC4 into ECX, tests it, stores [esp+4] into 0x005C8BD4, and if ECX is non-zero pushes the two arguments and calls USER32!SetWindowTextA through IAT 0x005331DC.

At 0x0048FA45, inside the window procedure at 0x0048F970, the getter is called in the WM_SYSKEYDOWN (0x0104) path after a VK_F4 (0x0073) comparison and a non-zero test of 0x005C8E04; the result is pushed directly as the first argument of USER32!PostMessageA. With the three preceding pushes (0,0,2) the call is PostMessageA(getter(), 0x0002, 0, 0).
observed_facts.evidence: C3; BN decompile of 0x48f970; r2 disassembly of 0x48f9b2-0x48fa57

observed_facts.fact: Only 0x0048FA45 is fully classified in this corrected pass. The other 19 call sites were not classified.
Binary Ninja types 0x005C8BC4 as int32_t and 0x006E5BC4 as int16_t data variables. These are database types and annotations, not retail source-level declarations.

expression_level_conclusion.statement: For the HWND expression at 0x0048FA45 only, retail calls a helper whose entire body is a read of the 32-bit global 0x005C8BC4. A candidate that supplies its corresponding window-handle value directly to PostMessageA is therefore equivalent at that expression, provided the candidate value equals the retail dword at the moment of the call.
expression_level_conclusion.proved: the helper is literally one absolute dword load followed by ret; the loaded dword is the value stored from the CreateWindowExA result at 0x0048F7A0
not_proved: window creation, lifetime, ownership, destruction order
that 0x005C8BC4 is non-null at every one of the 20 call sites
thread affinity of the window handle
equivalence for the other 19 call sites
semantics of any candidate g_window_handle variable

hypotheses.hypothesis: 0x005C8BC4 is the main-window handle for the period after 0x0048F7A0 until shutdown.
hypotheses.basis: It is written from the CreateWindowExA result, read for SetWindowTextA, and posted to for WM_DESTROY.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The original source exposed a getter rather than inlining the load, and the getter survived compilation as a distinct function.
hypotheses.basis: No evidence; the PE provides no source-level name.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A candidate g_window_handle variable corresponds to retail 0x005C8BC4.
hypotheses.basis: Suggested by the store/read pattern; candidate source was outside this task's scope and was not reviewed here.
hypotheses.status: inference for a later candidate comparison

unresolved.item: The purpose and full context of 19 of the 20 call sites are unclassified; only 0x0048FA45 is fully classified.
Whether 0x005C8BC4 can be null at each call site, and what each caller does with a null handle, is not established.
Window lifetime, ownership and destruction ordering are not established by this record.
Thread affinity: whether every call site runs on the thread that created the window is unknown.
A computed indirect call to 0x0048F0A0 cannot be excluded by a literal scan, although no address literal equal to the VA exists in the file.
The function has no symbol name in the retail PE; 'window-handle getter' is descriptive, and AppContext_GethWnd is a Binary Ninja database annotation.

limitations: Static analysis only. No runtime, behavioural or paired retail/candidate evidence exists for this record, and none is implied.

The earlier pass used Ghidra 12.1.2 because the Binary Ninja MCP endpoint had returned no_active_binary_view at that time. Binary Ninja MCP was reachable for this corrected pass and is the single decompiler used here. The earlier Ghidra output is retained only as superseded history and is not used for any conclusion.

The earlier pass's 6-byte size and instruction sequence for this VA were correct. The incorrect sizes produced by the earlier pass were for 0x00498460 (17 bytes instead of 23) and for 0x004010B0 (306 bytes instead of 28); this record's correction is tooling attribution and Binary Ninja confirmation, not a byte-size correction.
No candidate source was reviewed or compared, and no CFG-similarity score or structural-verification claim is made.
The function name is descriptive only; the retail PE provides no source-level name for this address.

The byte census of callers covers direct E8/E9/EB encodings in the .text section and stored dword literals equal to the target VA across the whole file. It cannot rule out an indirect call whose address is computed rather than stored as a literal.
objdump emits AT&T syntax (source, destination order); the Intel-style listings in this record come from Binary Ninja and radare2.
Binary Ninja's data-xref query returned 0 rows for 0x005C8BC4. The three-reference count is established by the byte-exact scan, objdump and radare2, not by BN data xrefs.
The 20-caller count is a direct-call census, not a full call-graph classification.
No runtime value of the HWND, no thread state and no candidate equivalence were observed.
